MUSDB

MUSDB18 results on 20 mixed songs (44.1 kHz stereo) from the test set, probing long-form music watermarking under the listed transformations. This setting is particularly challenging, as the 44.1 kHz sample rate differs from the native sample rate of all evaluated models and requires downsampling our model from its native 48 kHz.

Transformation Parameters

The transformations align to AudioSeal and XAttnMark for the selection and parameterization, with the sample rate adapted to the test set’s original sample rate whenever relevant. Additionally, cropping and vocoder attacks are added. The full list of parameterizations are specified below.

  • Identity: No transformation is applied.
  • AAC: AAC compression at 128 kbps.
  • MP3: MP3 compression at 128 kbps.
  • EnCodec: Neural codec compression using 16 codebooks (n_q=16), with audio resampled through 24 kHz.
  • RandomNoise: Additive Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.001.
  • PinkNoise: Additive pink noise with standard deviation 0.01.
  • VolumeChange: Scale the waveform by -20% or +20%, corresponding to multiplicative factors of 0.8 and 1.2.
  • EchoEffect: Add a delayed copy of the audio with delay and volume sampled between 0.1 and 0.5.
  • SmoothEffect: Applies moving average smoothing with deterministic windows of 2-10.
  • LowpassFilter: Remove frequencies above 5 kHz.
  • HighpassFilter: Remove frequencies below 500 Hz.
  • BandpassFilter: Retain frequencies between 300 Hz and 8 kHz.
  • Resample: Resample to an intermediate rate, and return to the original sample rate. The test includes two intermediate sample rates, 96 kHz and 16 kHz, where the results were aggregated.
  • SpeedAdjust: Change playback speed using randomized factors in [0.9, 1.1].
  • PitchShift: Shift pitch by -2, -1, +1, or +2 semitones.
  • Crop: Randomly remove $x\in[1, 400]$ samples from the beginning of the audio signal and zero-pad at the end
  • VocoderAttack: Convert the audio to magnitude spectrogram, and then reconstruct the waveform using the HiFT vocoder
